## 5b.5. Differential abundance analysis (pseudobulk-level)

> **Decision checkpoint** (enable above: `run_pseudobulk`)  
> Pseudobulk aggregates CLR abundance to **mean per `sample_alias` × cell type**, then fits limma across samples. Needs ≥2 samples per `condition`. Sample-level tables are written as `summary_abundance_data.rds` (and `.csv`); limma results as `differential_abundance_analysis.rds`.

```{r}
#| label: resp_statistical_testing_pseudobulk_abundance

if (isTRUE(pseudobulk_ok)) {
  # For each cell type: mean CLR per sample, then limma
  abundance_pseudobulk_parts <-
    names(markers_to_test) |>
    map(function(cell_type) {
      tryCatch(
        {
          markers_vec <- setdiff(
            as.character(unname(markers_to_test[[cell_type]])),
            c("sample_alias", "condition", "cell_id")
          )
          obj <- subset(pg_data, cell_annotation == cell_type)
          dat <- pseudobulk_fetch_abundance(obj, markers_vec)
          n_cells <- dat |>
            dplyr::count(
              .data$sample_alias,
              .data$condition,
              name = "n_cells"
            ) |>
            filter(n_cells >= pseudobulk_min_cells)
          if (nrow(n_cells) < 2) {
            return(NULL)
          }
          agg <- dat |>
            filter(.data$sample_alias %in% n_cells$sample_alias) |>
            pivot_longer(
              all_of(markers_vec),
              names_to = "marker",
              values_to = "clr"
            ) |>
            group_by(.data$sample_alias, .data$condition, .data$marker) |>
            summarise(mean_clr = mean(clr, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
            mutate(group = cell_type)
          fit <- run_pseudobulk_limma(
            agg,
            feature_col = "marker",
            value_col = "mean_clr",
            reference_condition = reference_condition,
            metadata = metadata,
            covariate_cols = pseudobulk_covariate_cols,
            block_col = pseudobulk_block_col,
            label = cell_type
          )
          list(
            agg = agg,
            res = if (nrow(fit$res) == 0) {
              NULL
            } else {
              fit$res |>
                rename(marker = feature) |>
                mutate(group = cell_type)
            }
          )
        },
        error = function(e) {
          message(paste(
            "Pseudobulk abundance error for",
            cell_type,
            ":",
            e$message
          ))
          NULL
        }
      )
    })

  # Save the sample-level means used as limma input
  summary_abundance_data_pseudobulk <- abundance_pseudobulk_parts |>
    map("agg") |>
    bind_rows()
  if (nrow(summary_abundance_data_pseudobulk) > 0) {
    save_pseudobulk_results(
      summary_abundance_data_pseudobulk,
      "abundance",
      "summary_abundance_data"
    )
  }

  differential_abundance_analysis_pseudobulk <- abundance_pseudobulk_parts |>
    map("res") |>
    bind_rows()

  if (nrow(differential_abundance_analysis_pseudobulk) > 0) {
    differential_abundance_analysis_pseudobulk <-
      adjust_contrast_fdr(differential_abundance_analysis_pseudobulk)
  }

  save_diff_results(
    differential_abundance_analysis_pseudobulk,
    "abundance",
    "pseudobulk",
    "differential_abundance_analysis"
  )
}
```

## 5b.6. Differential clustering analysis (pseudobulk-level)

Self-proximity (`marker_1 == marker_2`) from the shared sample-level table below, then limma. Column `diff_median` stores the limma logFC (mean difference) for schema compatibility with §5b.2.

The next chunk builds **one** proximity summary for both clustering and colocalization: `FilterProximityScores()` drops pairs below an isotype-derived background, then `SummarizeProximityScores()` takes the mean `log2_ratio` per `sample_alias` × cell type (missing cells as 0). That table is saved as `summary_proximity_data.rds` under both `clustering/pseudobulk/` and `colocalization/pseudobulk/`.

```{r}
#| label: resp_statistical_testing_pseudobulk_proximity_summary

if (isTRUE(pseudobulk_ok)) {
  # Background threshold for weak pairs: median isotype fraction + 2 MAD
  # (minimum 0.001), matching the usual pixelatorR spatial-analysis rule
  if ("isotype_fraction" %in% colnames(pg_data[[]])) {
    pseudobulk_proximity_background_pct <- max(
      median(pg_data$isotype_fraction, na.rm = TRUE) +
        2 * mad(pg_data$isotype_fraction, na.rm = TRUE),
      0.001
    )
  } else {
    message(
      "isotype_fraction missing from object metadata; ",
      "using FilterProximityScores background_threshold_pct = 0.001"
    )
    pseudobulk_proximity_background_pct <- 0.001
  }
  message(
    "FilterProximityScores background_threshold_pct = ",
    signif(pseudobulk_proximity_background_pct, 3)
  )

  summary_proximity_data_pseudobulk <-
    names(markers_to_test) |>
    map(function(cell_type) {
      tryCatch(
        {
          agg <- pseudobulk_summarize_proximity(
            subset(pg_data, cell_annotation == cell_type),
            markers_to_test[[cell_type]],
            background_threshold_pct = pseudobulk_proximity_background_pct
          )
          if (is.null(agg)) {
            return(NULL)
          }
          agg |> mutate(group = cell_type)
        },
        error = function(e) {
          message(
            paste(
              "Pseudobulk proximity summary error for",
              cell_type,
              ":",
              e$message
            )
          )
          NULL
        }
      )
    }) |>
    bind_rows()

  if (nrow(summary_proximity_data_pseudobulk) == 0) {
    message(
      "No sample-level proximity summaries; ",
      "clustering and colocalization pseudobulk tests will be skipped."
    )
  } else {
    # Same table is used for clustering and colocalization; save under both
    save_pseudobulk_results(
      summary_proximity_data_pseudobulk,
      "clustering",
      "summary_proximity_data"
    )
    save_pseudobulk_results(
      summary_proximity_data_pseudobulk,
      "colocalization",
      "summary_proximity_data"
    )
  }
}
```

) {

    run_pseudobulk_proximity_modality(

      self_pairs = TRUE,
      modality = "clustering",
      basename = "differential_clustering_analysis"
    )
}

## 5b.8. Pseudobulk diagnostics

Two tables recording what the pseudobulk fits actually did, both written under
`results_cleaned/05b_statistical_testing_response/pseudobulk_diagnostics/`:

- `skipped_tests.csv` — every fit or individual contrast that did not run, with
  the reason and the conditions that were missing. A contrast is dropped for a
  cell type when one of its conditions has no sample left after the
  `pseudobulk_min_cells` filter, so read this next to the §5b.4.1 table.
- `duplicate_correlation.csv` — the `duplicateCorrelation` consensus per fit.
  A fit is absent from this table when no donor contributed more than one
  surviving sample, in which case it was fitted without blocking.

```{r}
#| label: resp_statistical_testing_pseudobulk_diagnostics

if (isTRUE(pseudobulk_ok)) {
  diagnostics_dir <- here::here(
    "pna_b1b2",
    "results_cleaned/05b_statistical_testing_response/pseudobulk_diagnostics"
  )
  dir.create(diagnostics_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

  pseudobulk_skipped_tests <- collect_pseudobulk_diagnostics("skips")
  if (nrow(pseudobulk_skipped_tests) > 0) {
    message("Pseudobulk fits skipped:")
    print(as.data.frame(pseudobulk_skipped_tests))
  } else {
    message("No pseudobulk fits were skipped.")
  }
  write.csv(
    pseudobulk_skipped_tests,
    file.path(diagnostics_dir, "skipped_tests.csv"),
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  pseudobulk_dupcor_table <- collect_pseudobulk_diagnostics("dupcor")
  if (nrow(pseudobulk_dupcor_table) > 0) {
    message("duplicateCorrelation consensus per fit:")
    print(as.data.frame(pseudobulk_dupcor_table))
  } else {
    message("No blocked fits were run, so there is no consensus correlation.")
  }
  write.csv(
    pseudobulk_dupcor_table,
    file.path(diagnostics_dir, "duplicate_correlation.csv"),
    row.names = FALSE
  )
}
```

## 5b.9. Restore full objects

The subset objects are replaced with the full ones saved at the start of this module, so any module run afterwards in the same session (or in the full-report render) sees all samples and the original `condition` column.

```{r}

pg_data <- pg_data_all
metadata <- metadata_all
condition_palette <- condition_palette_all
rm(pg_data_all, metadata_all, condition_palette_all)
```
